purpose: Five documented residential-lease security-cheque court cases with access-level and judicial-finding boundaries; no automatic rules or fixture answers.

judicial_evidence.finding: Landlord completed a signed security cheque for ILS 146,000. Court found the completion exceeded the contractually authorized security scope and failed the good-faith requirement.
Evidence about reported defects and disputed renovations was examined separately; the security-note enforcement claim was dismissed.

cases.possible_model_error: Treat a blank signed security cheque as an unlimited authorization or pool every alleged landlord loss into the cheque.
cases.limits: Specific 2018 tenancy, 2024 lower-court judgment and evidence; not a general cap calculation, bank presentment rule, or automated result for other leases.

judicial_evidence.finding: A security cheque for ILS 4,000 led to objection and a substantially larger amended contractual damages claim. The displayed reasoning says the landlord then had to prove the contractual claim rather than rely on the cheque's evidentiary presumptions.
The court's displayed reasoning accepted the tenant's account that handwritten no-pets conditions were added after signing; party testimony and messages were assessed.

cases.possible_model_error: Treat later handwritten text as part of the signed agreement without checking authenticity, or transfer bill-of-exchange proof advantages to a later amended contract lawsuit.
cases.limits: Only web-indexed excerpts were accessible; final amount, all findings and official court original still require direct verification.

judicial_evidence.finding: Court read the third-party cheque's wording alongside landlord-tenant conduct during successive renewals; it rejected the claimed rent-and-tax-only restriction and found a wider agreed security scope.
Damage assessment, expert evidence and unsupported utility amounts were treated separately. Indexed disposition reports a partly allowed claim of ILS 27,244.

cases.possible_model_error: Infer a third-party security cheque expires after the original term or covers only taxes from the 'non-negotiable' note, without inspecting renewals and correspondence.
cases.limits: 2015 pre-2017 decision, indexed transcript only because full mirrored page was unavailable; original judgment and any appeal not independently retrieved.

judicial_evidence.finding: The lease contemplated a promissory note, guaranty and security cheque, but only the security cheque was actually delivered. The court expressly rejected the argument that the 'security cheque' inscription itself invalidated the cheque as a bill of exchange.
The court read the instrument alongside broader lease sections instead of accepting a taxes-only interpretation merely from one phrase.

cases.possible_model_error: Treat 'security cheque' inscription as a bank or bill-of-exchange block, or invent extra security instruments promised but never delivered.
cases.limits: Only beginning and selected reasoning of mirrored judgment visible; the overall result cannot be reported from this source; predates 2017 rental reform.

judicial_evidence.locator: intro; reasoning on termination and mitigation; disposition
judicial_evidence.finding: A blank security cheque was later filled for three months' alleged unpaid rent. Court accepted evidence of an early impediment to residing in the dwelling and the tenant's termination; conditions to complete and collect the security cheque were not met.
Court dismissed both claims, ordered the cheque execution file closed, and also considered the landlord's four-month delay in re-letting.

cases.possible_model_error: Treat the completion or dishonour of a blank cheque as proof the underlying secured obligation became due; ignore early termination and mitigation evidence.
cases.limits: 2011 pre-2017 fact-specific magistrates decision; not an automatic interpretation of present-day §25י.

gaps: Official judiciary-hosted complete originals and later appeal history not checked for any of the five cases.
One judgment's final disposition not accessible; two outcomes documented in search-index transcripts requiring original verification.
Do not copy mirrored judgments into a public fixture or convert these observations into expert-verified rules; preserve train/evaluation isolation.
